newsitem.title: USA: Washington state jobless rate dips to 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Washington state jobless rate dips to 6.2 pct.

text.p: A surging Puget Sound economy pulled Washington State's jobless rate down two-tenths of a percentage point to 6.2 percent in January, state officials said Tuesday.
The January rate was the lowest for the month since 1990, state Employment Security Commissioner Carver Gayton said.

"A sharp speed-up in the economy, which began late last year, carried forward into the new year," Gayton said in a statement. "This is not typical for January and indicates real growth in the economy."

Nonfarm wage and salary employment fell seasonally by 55,500 workers, less than the 64,000 average over the past four years. Manufacturing employment dropped 2,500. Lumber and wood products fell 400. Food processing scaled back 900.
"The one significant counter to this trend was a 1,400-worker gain in aircraft and parts," said Dennis Fusco, chief economist for the state Employment Security Department.

Construction payrolls dropped 7,600 workers -- almost 2,000 less than the average of the past four years. Post-Christmas layoffs drove wholesale and retail trade down by 27,000. Services employment dropped 10,100 compared to 12,400 last year, the department said.
